name: Jump Core
description: The jump verb, with the two forgiveness windows that make it feel fair. Coyote time accepts a press shortly after walking off an edge; the jump buffer accepts a press shortly before landing and fires it on touchdown. Both exist because a jump that only answers a frame-perfect press reads as broken input rather than as difficulty. maxJumps covers double and triple jumps on one counter, reset by movement.grounded. airControlFraction governs steering while airborne, which is a jump concern rather than a locomotion one: it is the difference between a committed leap aimed entirely at takeoff and a jump that can be redirected in flight, and it has no meaning in a build with no jump. This component emits no landing event — movement.ground_sensor already does, and a second source for one fact doubles every count downstream.

inputs.name: jumpVelocity
inputs.description: Upward speed applied at takeoff. Against movement.physics_core's default gravity of 9.8 this apexes at roughly 4 units; the pair must be tuned together, since raising gravity alone shortens the jump.

inputs.name: maxJumps
inputs.description: Total jumps before touching ground. 1 is a ground jump only; 2 is a double jump.

inputs.name: coyoteTimeSeconds
inputs.description: How long after leaving walkable ground a first jump is still accepted. Measured against ground_sensor's timeSinceGrounded. Consumes a jump, so it cannot be stacked with an air jump for extra height.

inputs.name: jumpBufferSeconds
inputs.description: How long a press is remembered while airborne, fired on the next landing. The buffer is cleared when consumed so one press can never produce two jumps.

inputs.name: airControlFraction
inputs.description: How much horizontal steering the player keeps while airborne, as a fraction of ground control. 0 is a committed jump; 1 is full mid-air redirection. The interesting values are in between, and this is the single knob that most decides whether a jump feels heavy or floaty.

inputs.name: variableHeight
inputs.description: Whether releasing the jump input mid-rise cuts the jump short.

inputs.name: releaseVelocityMultiplier
inputs.description: What rising velocity is scaled to on early release. Only read when variableHeight is true. 0 stops the rise dead, which reads as a hitch.

outputs.name: isJumping
outputs.description: True from takeoff until the rise ends, not for the whole airborne period.
